script.title: Forfeiture and Reissue of Shares
script.caption_hook: They cancel your shares but keep your money? Here's how forfeiture works.

lines.say: Ma'am, company cancels my shares but keeps my money? How's that fair?
If a member doesn't pay a call, the company cancels the shares. Money already received stays.
Say 100 shares of ₹10. Called up ₹8, paid ₹6. Unpaid ₹2 each is ₹200, calls in arrear.
Okay, and how do we record that?
Debit share capital ₹800, the called-up amount. Credit forfeited shares ₹600 and calls in arrear ₹200.
Can they sell those shares again?
Yes! Reissue them as fully paid ₹10 shares at ₹7. Bank gets ₹700; ₹300 discount comes from forfeited shares.
Can they give any discount they want?
Only up to the amount forfeited on those shares. Here ₹600, so ₹300 is fine.
Where does the leftover forfeited money go?
Capital reserve equals forfeited amount minus discount. ₹600 minus ₹300 is ₹300.

board.title: Capital Reserve
board.sub: F = amount forfeited, D = discount on reissue

lines.say: Oh! So it goes to Capital Reserve, not profit?
Yes. Debit forfeited shares, credit capital reserve ₹300.
Remember: paid stays, unpaid goes. Forfeit first, then reissue!

check_notes: Writer: Example: 100 shares of ₹10, called up ₹8, paid ₹6. Forfeiture: Share Capital Dr 800, Forfeited Shares 600, Calls in Arrear 200. Reissue at ₹7 as fully paid: Bank 700, Forfeited Shares Dr 300, Share Capital 1,000. Capital Reserve 600 − 300 = 300. Calc board label now reads "Arrear 100×(₹8−₹6)" (18-character limit), and the voice line says ₹200 is calls in arrear.

Checker: Line 2 (voice): 'If a member doesn't pay a call, the company cancels the shares' makes forfeiture sound automatic. Forfeiture is optional. It needs authority in the Articles (Table F), a notice of at least 14 days to the defaulting member, and a board resolution. Suggested wording: 'If a member doesn't pay a call even after notice, the company may forfeit the shares as its Articles allow. Money already received stays with the company.'

Checker: Line 12 (board formula F − D): the sub-text should make clear that this applies only to shares that have been reissued. Suggested wording: 'F = amount forfeited on the shares reissued, D = discount on reissue.' The ₹300 result is correct here because all 100 shares were reissued, but with a partial reissue the formula as written would give the wrong figure.
